name: ghost
reason: Large mixed JavaScript and TypeScript monorepo (about 9k files). Scale benchmark for BA-28/BA-17: wall time and peak memory of a full analysis. Budgets are the measured run plus 10% (S1 no-regression rule). Measured 2026-11-03 after the BA-17 memory pass (16-core Windows 11, Bun 1.4.4): 7,174 of 9,171 files analyzed, 328 s wall time, 6,166 MiB peak RSS, 1.6 GB output. Earlier: 768 s and 11,431 MiB after Wave 3; about 26 min in the audit-era run (2026-10-29). ADR-009 (2026-11-04, #253-#257): 1,847 MiB peak in a same-session A/B (main before: 2,613 MiB; 9,878 MiB before ADR-009). The memory budget is that peak plus about 40% for GC variance; wall time stays at 360 s until it is re-measured on a cool machine. NA-04 (2026-11-08): the gate now measures a fresh analysis only (an earlier .discovery is removed, a snapshot reuse is refused) and the engine alone (time and peak memory when the engine returns, before the harness re-reads ~930 MB of output). Two idle runs on b29d8ac+NA-01/02: 216 s / 1,677 MiB and 253 s / 2,213 MiB. A snapshot reuse of Ghost peaked at 8,939 MiB (NA-16), which is why earlier same-cache runs read 9-10 GB. ADR-011 (2026-11-09, #285 and #286): reuse now peaks at 936-1,006 MiB in about 25 s, one engine process per run (main before: 11,610 MiB, 79 s); a fresh run that day: 183 s, 2,417 MiB.
